sentences.text: Based on related family members, Pectinodon was likely a small, bird-like, feathered bipedal dinosaur with large eyes and brains.
Its teeth are small, measuring less than 1 cm in crown height, and feature large triangular denticles on the distal edge.
The genus name Pectinodon means "comb tooth" because the teeth have comb-like serrations on their rear edges.
The holotype specimen UCM 38445 is a single adult tooth measuring 6.2 mm in length.
Kenneth Carpenter named the species Pectinodon bakkeri in 1982 based on theropod teeth found in the Lance Formation of Wyoming.
The specific name bakkeri honors the paleontologist Robert Thomas Bakker.
The morphology of Pectinodon's teeth suggests it preferred soft prey such as invertebrates, small vertebrates, or carrion.
Some researchers speculate that troodontids, including Pectinodon, were omnivorous based on their tooth morphology.
A study using stable isotopes in tooth enamel reaffirmed the hypothesis that troodontids were omnivorous.
Pectinodon lived at the end of the Maastrichtian age of the Late Cretaceous period, approximately 66 million years ago.
The genus Pectinodon has a time range extending from the Cenomanian to the Maastrichtian, between 100.5 and 66 million years ago.
It is debated whether numerous Late Cretaceous specimens assigned to Troodon formosus represent new species, though a thorough review is still required.
